title: Term-Completion Relief on TRAC Deficiencies under the Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease
content:
# Training Q&A — Term Relief on a TRAC Deficiency, Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease

**Rule.** For the deficiency billed on a TRAC unit of the Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease whose sale settlement falls short of its book value, the deficiency term relief is 10 percent where the unit had been in service for at least its scheduled term in whole months when it was turned in, 5 percent where it had been in service 24 or more whole months but less than its scheduled term, and nothing where it had been in service fewer than 24 whole months.

**Q. How is time in service measured?**
A. In whole months from the unit's in-service date to its turn-in date (for a recovered unit, the recovery date the unit records). Whole months are one fewer where the turn-in date's day of the month is smaller than the in-service date's.

**Q. What is the scheduled term?**
A. The term in months on the unit's schedule.

**Q. What does each case give?**

| Whole months in service at turn-in | Term relief |
|---|---|
| at least the scheduled term | 10 percent |
| 24 or more, but less than the scheduled term | 5 percent |
| fewer than 24, and less than the scheduled term | nothing |

**Q. Some cases? (hypothetical)**
A.
- Scheduled term 36 months, 36 whole months in service: 10 percent. 35 whole months: 5 percent.
- Scheduled term 36 months, 24 whole months: 5 percent; 23 whole months: nothing.
- Scheduled term 18 months, 20 whole months in service: at least the scheduled term, 10 percent.
